title: Memory without regret
brief: The assistant should remember things across sessions, but the personalization value, the delete rules, the network posture and the trust in whatever gets written are all undecided. Decide what to store, who may write it and how it is read back.

blocks.text: Memory types, policies and the attack surface

blocks.caption: CoALA separates working memory from three long-term types [[r28]]. MemGPT adds the idea of virtual context management across memory tiers [[r29]].
head: Type
What it holds
Typical write
Typical read
rows: The live context window: task, recent turns, scratchpad
After a session, or on an explicit remember command
Retrieve by similarity or recency when a similar situation recurs
Durable facts about the user, the domain or the world
At session start or per turn
Rules and how-to steps for recurring workflows

items: **Write policies:** an explicit user command, extraction at the end of a session, or background consolidation that merges duplicates and resolves contradictions.
**Read policies:** load a profile once at session start, retrieve summaries on every turn, or let the agent call a memory tool on demand.

**Foundry Agent Service memory (preview, checked 2026-10-13)** names three types, all enabled by default: user profile (retrieved at conversation start), chat summary (retrieved per turn) and procedural (retrieved for recurring workflows). It works in three phases: extraction, consolidation and retrieval [[r13]].

**Claude's memory tool** is client side: Claude requests file operations under `/memories` and your application executes them, so path traversal protection is your job. Its GA status was not stated on the page when checked [[r41]].

steps.title: Candidate
steps.md: The agent or an extractor proposes a memory from the conversation.

steps.title: Screen
steps.md: Scan for injection, PII and policy. Reject instruction-like text.

steps.title: Consolidate
steps.md: Merge duplicates, resolve contradictions, add provenance and a TTL.

steps.title: Store with scope
steps.md: Tenant and user scope on every record, plus a delete handle.

steps.title: Retrieve
steps.md: Top-k within scope. Show age and source and treat the text as data, not instructions.

blocks.title: Design the memory layer
blocks.prompt: Flip the dials. Stateless is on the board because it wins when personalization is worth little.

blocks.takeaway: Treat every memory write as untrusted input. The less you trust the writers, the more a gate and a delete path matter.

items.symptom: The assistant pushes a recommendation or link no one asked for, across many users
items.cause: Poisoned memory. MINJA plants records through ordinary queries with no direct write access [[r23]]. AgentPoison reports above 80% attack success at a poison rate below 0.1% [[r24]].
items.fix: Screen every write, keep provenance, treat recalled text as data, and run adversarial tests. Foundry's docs advise Content Safety prompt-injection detection plus adversarial testing [[r13]].

items.symptom: A user asks to be forgotten and an old preference still appears
items.cause: Derived summaries survive, or records are not tied to a deletable scope
items.fix: Scope every record, support item-level delete and TTL, delete derived artifacts and test deletion end to end.

items.symptom: One tenant's fact appears for another tenant
items.cause: Scope missing or shared on retrieval
items.fix: Make scope mandatory on every read and write. Foundry's low-level APIs require an explicit `scope`. Test with cross-scope probes.

items.symptom: The assistant keeps citing an outdated fact
items.cause: No consolidation or recency handling, so contradictions pile up
items.fix: Consolidate on write, store timestamps, prefer the newest record and expire with a TTL.

items.symptom: Latency and tokens per turn climb as memory grows
items.cause: Too many memories retrieved every turn
items.fix: Cap top-k, load the profile once per session and retrieve per-turn summaries only when needed.

blocks.title: Foundry memory limits, preview as of 2026-10-13
blocks.md: 100 scopes per store, 10,000 memories per scope, and 1,000 search plus 1,000 update requests per minute. It needs compatible Azure OpenAI chat and embedding deployments and does not support VNet integration. The latest preview added item-level create, read, update and delete, a store default TTL and direct remember-or-forget commands [[r13]]. Mem0 reports 91% lower p95 latency and over 90% token savings against a full-context baseline on LOCOMO, but the paper is vendor-authored [[r40]].

quiz.q: Match each memory type to what it stores.

pairs.r: The contents of the live context window
Durable facts about a user or a domain
Rules and how-to steps for recurring workflows

quiz.explain: The CoALA split ties each type to a different read pattern: working memory is always in context, episodic is recalled by situation, semantic by topic and procedural by workflow.

quiz.q: Researchers show an attacker can plant malicious memory records through ordinary queries, with no direct write access to the memory store. Which control addresses that path?
options: Encrypt the memory store at rest with a customer-managed key so the planted records cannot be read
Restrict the memory API so that only administrators can create records, and keep the agent read-only
Screen every write as untrusted input and test adversarially
Raise the embedding dimension so that poisoned records separate from genuine ones
quiz.explain: The agent writes memories on the user's behalf, so the attack arrives through normal use. Screening, provenance and adversarial testing address that. Encryption at rest does not stop poisoned content, an admin-only API breaks the agent's own writes without screening them, and a larger embedding does not detect malicious text.

quiz.q: Personalization is valuable, and the security team requires private-network-only access for the agent's data services. Which choice changes, and why?
options: Managed Foundry memory stays the best choice because it is the only option that includes extraction
A client-side or self-hosted store, since Foundry memory has no VNet support as of 2026-10-13
Fall back to thread state only, because personalization is impossible once the network is isolated
Keep Foundry memory and raise its scope limit
quiz.explain: The Foundry memory page lists VNet integration as unsupported in preview, so an isolation requirement moves you to a store you can place inside the network. Thread-only memory gives up the value you wanted, and the scope limit has nothing to do with network posture.

takeaways: Name the memory type before you pick a store: working, episodic, semantic or procedural.
Design the write path first: screen, consolidate, scope, then retrieve.
Every write is untrusted input. MINJA and AgentPoison show poisoning without direct write access.
Foundry memory is preview with limits and no VNet support as of 2026-10-13. Isolation or strict deletion rules can flip you to a store you control.
